guidance: Planning sequence only. Timing assumes every call in a tier starts together, lasts the entered call length and reaches the person; an unanswered call delays the branch below it. No phone numbers are collected and no message is sent.
method: The first name on the roster is the coordinator. The tree is filled level by level: the coordinator phones the next b names, those callers phone the next b names each, and so on, where b is the calls-per-person figure. A queue walk assigns every remaining name to the earliest caller with an unused slot, so the tree is balanced and no name is skipped. The depth is the number of tiers, which is the smallest t for which 1 + b + b squared + ... + b^t is at least the roster size; the capacity reported is that full geometric sum. Every tier's calls are assumed to happen at once, so the elapsed time is one call length per tier and the time to the last person is tiers times the call length. Everyone except the coordinator is called exactly once, so the call count is the roster size minus one. The busiest tier is the tier with the most calls. Rosters are limited to 60 names, names to 40 characters, call lengths to whole minutes from 1 to 60 and calls per person to whole numbers from 1 to 8; blank lines are ignored and repeated names are refused without regard to case.
